Acrobatic Maneuver.oracle_text:
Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.
Draw a card.

Angelic Ascension.oracle_text: Exile target creature or planeswalker. Its controller creates a 4/4 white Angel creature token with flying.

Angelic Page.oracle_text:
Flying
{T}: Target attacking or blocking creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

Anointed Chorister.oracle_text:
Lifelink (Damage dealt by this creature also causes you to gain that much life.)
{4}{W}: This creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn.

Baneslayer Angel.oracle_text: Flying, first strike, lifelink, protection from Demons and from Dragons

Basri's Acolyte.oracle_text:
Lifelink (Damage dealt by this creature also causes you to gain that much life.)
When this creature enters, put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to two other target creatures you control.

Blessed Sanctuary.oracle_text:
Prevent all noncombat damage that would be dealt to you and creatures you control.
Whenever a nontoken creature you control enters, create a 2/2 white Unicorn creature token.

Brightmare.oracle_text: When this creature enters, tap up to one target creature. You gain life equal to that creature's power.

Bulwark Giant.oracle_text: When this creature enters, you gain 5 life.

Cloudshift.oracle_text: Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under your control.

Daybreak Charger.oracle_text: When this creature enters, target creature gets +2/+0 until end of turn.

Distinguished Conjurer.oracle_text:
Whenever another creature you control enters, you gain 1 life.
{4}{W}, {T}: Exile another target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control.

Emancipation Angel.oracle_text:
Flying
When this creature enters, return a permanent you control to its owner's hand.

Emiel the Blessed.oracle_text:
{3}: Exile another target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control.
Whenever another creature you control enters, you may pay {G/W}. If you do, put a +1/+1 counter on it. If it's a Unicorn, put two +1/+1 counters on it instead. ({G/W} can be paid with either {G} or {W}.)

Faith's Fetters.oracle_text:
Enchant permanent
When this Aura enters, you gain 4 life.
Enchanted permanent can't attack or block, and its activated abilities can't be activated unless they're mana abilities.

Feat of Resistance.oracle_text: Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. It gains protection from the color of your choice until end of turn. (It can't be blocked, targeted, dealt damage, enchanted, or equipped by anything of that color.)

Flicker of Fate.oracle_text: Exile target creature or enchantment, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control.

Griffin Aerie.oracle_text: At the beginning of your end step, if you gained 3 or more life this turn, create a 2/2 white Griffin creature token with flying.

Inspired Charge.oracle_text: Creatures you control get +2/+1 until end of turn.

Preston, the Vanisher.oracle_text:
Whenever another nontoken creature you control enters, if it wasn't cast, create a token that's a copy of that creature, except it's a 0/1 white Illusion.
{1}{W}, Sacrifice five Illusions: Exile target nonland permanent.

Revitalize.oracle_text:
You gain 3 life.
Draw a card.

Settle Beyond Reality.oracle_text:
Choose one or both —
• Exile target creature you don't control.
• Exile target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control.

Thraben Inspector.oracle_text: When this creature enters, investigate. (Create a Clue token. It's an artifact with "{2}, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card.")

Thriving Heath.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped. As it enters, choose a color other than white.
{T}: Add {W} or one mana of the chosen color.

Wispweaver Angel.oracle_text:
Flying
When this creature enters, you may exile another target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a 2-land hand that had a strong 2-drop (Distinguished Conjurer) and an incredibly powerful synergy engine (Conjurer + Blessed Sanctuary + Wispweaver Angel + Acrobatic Maneuver). While only having 2 lands is risky, the curve starts at 2 mana and the late-game synergy is exceptional for Limited.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Distinguished Conjurer on turn 2 is a solid start, and with ~75%+ chance to find a 3rd land by turn 3, the risk is manageable given the hand's enormous synergy potential. Mulliganing to 6 risks losing both card advantage and this powerful combination of cards.

annotations.description: Passed priority with Revitalize available and Griffin Aerie on the battlefield. Casting Revitalize would gain 3 life (triggering Griffin Aerie to create a 2/2 flyer at end step), draw a card, and use otherwise wasted mana. There's no reason to hold Revitalize here - the hand contains Baneslayer Angel and Bulwark Giant which can't be cast yet, and the extra card draw helps find lands to cast them sooner.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything, wasting mana and missing the Griffin Aerie trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Revitalize to gain 3 life, draw a card, and trigger Griffin Aerie at end step for a 2/2 flying token.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main phase with 3 untapped lands and Revitalize available to cast. Revitalize would gain 3 life (triggering Griffin Aerie to create a 2/2 flying Griffin token at end step), draw a card, and use mana that would otherwise be wasted. This is pure upside being left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 3 untapped lands and no action taken.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Revitalize to gain 3 life, draw a card, and trigger Griffin Aerie at end of turn to create a 2/2 flying Griffin token.

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach passed on casting Revitalize during combat when being attacked by a 3/1 Daybreak Charger. Casting Revitalize would have offset the 3 combat damage, drawn a card, and triggered Griffin Aerie at end step to create a 2/2 flying Griffin token. Instead, they took 3 damage for nothing and missed the Griffin Aerie trigger.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, taking 3 damage with no benefit.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Revitalize for {1}{W} to gain 3 life (netting even on life), draw a card, and trigger Griffin Aerie to create a 2/2 flying Griffin token at end of turn.

annotations.description: Chose Blue for Thriving Heath when the deck contains Emiel the Blessed, whose {G/W} trigger could benefit from Green mana. Blue has no apparent use in this mono-white deck. While the color choice on Thriving Heath is often low-impact, Green would have been strictly better given the known deck contents.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Blue for Thriving Heath's color
annotations.betterLine: Choose Green for Thriving Heath to have potential synergy with Emiel the Blessed's {G/W} ability if drawn later

annotations.description: Passed with 3 mana available and multiple castable spells. Most importantly, Revitalize would gain 3 life, draw a card, AND trigger Griffin Aerie at end step to create a 2/2 flying Griffin token. This is a significant missed opportunity for card advantage and board development.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, doing nothing with 3 available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Revitalize to gain 3 life, draw a card, and trigger Griffin Aerie for a 2/2 flying Griffin token at end of turn. Could also consider casting Angelic Page to develop the board.

annotations.description: Opponent has no untapped creatures (Preston is sick and can't block) and all lands are tapped. Both Anointed Chorister (2/2) and Basri's Acolyte (2/3) could attack for a free 4 damage with zero risk. Basri's Acolyte also has lifelink, gaining 2 life. There is absolutely no downside to attacking here.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without declaring any attackers, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Anointed Chorister and Basri's Acolyte for 4 unblockable damage and 2 life from lifelink. The opponent is completely tapped out with no available blockers.

annotations.description: Preston, the Vanisher is a dangerous engine that can generate token copies of ETB creatures and has a removal ability (sacrifice 5 Illusions to exile a nonland permanent). The opponent is completely tapped out, making this an ideal window to use Angelic Ascension on Preston. While giving the opponent a 4/4 flyer, Baneslayer Angel (5/5 flying, first strike, lifelink) can handle it easily. Leaving Preston alive risks the opponent generating significant value in future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting Angelic Ascension, leaving Preston, the Vanisher on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Angelic Ascension targeting Preston, the Vanisher while the opponent is tapped out. The resulting 4/4 Angel token is manageable with Baneslayer Angel, and removing Preston prevents a powerful value engine from taking over the game.

annotations.description: Player timed out on Emancipation Angel's mandatory bounce trigger, likely resulting in a suboptimal permanent being returned (probably Anointed Chorister, losing its +1/+1 counter). The board position with Baneslayer Angel is still strong, but value was lost.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response), letting the game auto-select a permanent to bounce.
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Basri's Acolyte to replay later for additional +1/+1 counter value, or bounce Griffin Aerie (cheap to replay at 2 mana) to preserve all creatures and counters on the battlefield.

annotations.description: Preston, the Vanisher is a significant threat that generates Illusion tokens from blink effects, eventually enabling its exile ability on nonland permanents. The opponent is fully tapped out, making this a safe window to use Angelic Ascension on Preston. The 4/4 Angel token the opponent would get is easily handled by Baneslayer Angel (5/5, flying, first strike, lifelink). However, saving Angelic Ascension for later threats is defensible given the strong board position.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting Emancipation Angel's bounce trigger resolve without casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Angelic Ascension targeting Preston, the Vanisher while the opponent is tapped out. The resulting 4/4 Angel token is dominated by Baneslayer Angel in combat, and removing Preston prevents future Illusion token generation and the exile ability.

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach declined to attack with any creatures when the opponent was completely tapped out with only Preston, the Vanisher 2/5 as a blocker. Basri's Acolyte (2/3 lifelink) is a completely risk-free attacker — it survives being blocked by Preston (takes 2, has 3 toughness) and gains life either way. Even attacking with both creatures guarantees 2-3 damage through since Preston can only block one. With the opponent at 23 life, every point of damage matters, especially since Gem3P Coach has Griffin Aerie which benefits from the lifelink triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with at least Basri's Acolyte (risk-free due to surviving Preston's 2 damage with its 3 toughness, plus lifelink synergy with Griffin Aerie). Ideally attack with both creatures — opponent is tapped out with no tricks available, guaranteeing 2-3 damage gets through.

annotations.description: Preston the Vanisher (2/5) could attack into an opponent with only Basri's Acolyte (2/3) and Anointed Chorister (2/2) as non-sick blockers. With all lands tapped on both sides, combat tricks are unlikely. Preston would survive any single block and kill the blocker, or survive a double block while killing one creature. Dealing 2 damage or trading favorably in combat would apply meaningful pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Preston, the Vanisher
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Preston, the Vanisher. It survives any single blocker and likely forces a favorable trade. Even if double-blocked, Preston survives at 1 toughness. With opponent's lands tapped, combat tricks are very unlikely. However, keeping Preston back to protect the combo engine is a reasonable alternative plan.

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach passed on attacking with flying creatures when the opponent was completely tapped out. Emancipation Angel (3/3 flying) and Angelic Page (1/1 flying) could attack for 4 unblockable damage since the only non-sick creature on opponent's side is Preston (2/5, no flying). Wispweaver Angel is sick and can't block. All opponent lands are tapped so there are zero combat tricks possible.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with at least Emancipation Angel and Angelic Page for 4 free flying damage. Could also send ground creatures since opponent can only block one with Preston (2/5), dealing additional damage. With opponent at 23 life, every point of pressure matters.

annotations.description: Failed to use Cloudshift on Wispweaver Angel to trigger Preston, the Vanisher's copy ability. Cloudshifting Wispweaver creates a chain: the real Wispweaver returns (Preston makes an Illusion copy), both Wispweavers' ETBs can flicker other creatures, generating multiple Illusion tokens. With the opponent's lands all tapped, there's no risk of interaction. This could rapidly accumulate toward Preston's 5-Illusion exile ability to remove Baneslayer Angel.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Cast Cloudshift targeting Wispweaver Angel to start the Preston/Wispweaver flicker chain, generating multiple Illusion tokens and potentially reaching 5 Illusions to exile Baneslayer Angel with Preston's activated ability.

annotations.description: Casting Cloudshift while Distinguished Conjurer is still on the stack means DC isn't on the battlefield when Wispweaver Angel re-enters. If they let DC resolve first, DC would see Wispweaver (and any further creatures) enter, triggering its 'gain 1 life' ability, and the Illusion copy of DC from Preston would also provide additional life gain triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Cloudshift in response to Distinguished Conjurer still on the stack, causing Wispweaver to re-enter before DC is on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Let Distinguished Conjurer resolve first, then cast Cloudshift targeting Wispweaver Angel. DC would see Wispweaver enter (gain 1 life), the Preston Illusion copy of DC would also trigger, and further blink chains would generate more value.

annotations.description: With Cloudshift on the stack and Preston, the Vanisher on the battlefield, declining to cast Flicker of Fate on another creature (like Distinguished Conjurer or Wispweaver Angel) misses generating additional ETB triggers and Illusion token copies from Preston. The mana was available (3 untapped Plains, Flicker costs {1}{W}) and the value would have been significant.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, declining to cast Flicker of Fate in response to Cloudshift on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Flicker of Fate targeting Distinguished Conjurer (or another creature) to get an additional Preston Illusion token copy and ETB triggers, maximizing the value of having Preston on the battlefield.

annotations.description: Flickering Preston with Wispweaver Angel's ETB doesn't generate an Illusion token because Preston's ability only triggers on 'another' creature entering. Flickering Distinguished Conjurer would have triggered Preston to create an Illusion copy of DC (progressing toward the 5-Illusion exile ability), and the returning DC would also trigger life gain from seeing future creatures enter.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to flicker Preston, the Vanisher with Wispweaver Angel's ETB
annotations.betterLine: Flicker Distinguished Conjurer to get an Illusion token from Preston's trigger, building toward the 5-Illusion exile ability while keeping the blink chain value higher

annotations.description: With Preston, the Vanisher and Distinguished Conjurer on the battlefield, casting Flicker of Fate on Wispweaver Angel would generate massive value: Preston creates an Illusion token copy of Wispweaver, Distinguished Conjurer gains life, and the re-entered Wispweaver's ETB could flicker another creature for even more Preston/Conjurer triggers. This builds toward Preston's 5-Illusion exile ability and generates significant board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Flicker of Fate while Preston triggers were on the stack, saving the 2 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Flicker of Fate targeting Wispweaver Angel (or Distinguished Conjurer) to generate additional Illusion tokens via Preston and life via Distinguished Conjurer, creating a chain of ETB value triggers.

annotations.description: Targeted the 0/1 Wispweaver Angel token with Wispweaver Angel's ETB flicker ability. Tokens that are exiled cease to exist and never return, so this wastes the trigger entirely — it just destroys their own token for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Wispweaver Angel 0/1 token, which will be permanently exiled (tokens cease to exist in exile).
annotations.betterLine: Target Distinguished Conjurer with the Wispweaver Angel ETB. It gets flickered and returns, triggering Preston to create a 0/1 Illusion copy of Distinguished Conjurer, and the original Conjurer then triggers on future creature entries for life gain. This generates actual value instead of destroying your own token.

annotations.description: The 0/1 Wispweaver Angel Illusion token has Wispweaver's ETB ability. Targeting the real Wispweaver Angel would create a flicker chain: real Wispweaver re-enters → Preston makes another Illusion copy of Wispweaver → real Wispweaver's ETB targets another creature → more triggers and tokens. Targeting Distinguished Conjurer instead gets only 1 life and 1 Illusion token, missing the opportunity for a much larger chain.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Distinguished Conjurer with the Wispweaver Illusion token's flicker ETB
annotations.betterLine: Target the real Wispweaver Angel (p69) to create a flicker chain, generating multiple Illusion tokens and ETB triggers for significantly more value.

annotations.description: All of the opponent's creatures have summoning sickness, meaning zero blockers are available. Attacking with only Baneslayer Angel deals 5 damage instead of 13 unblockable damage. This leaves 8 free damage on the table against an opponent at 32 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Baneslayer Angel for 5 damage (opponent goes to 27, player gains 5 life to 26).
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Baneslayer Angel, Emancipation Angel, Anointed Chorister, Basri's Acolyte, Angelic Page) for 13 unblockable damage since every opponent creature is summoning sick and cannot block. This would put opponent to 19 instead of 27.

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach declined to activate Angelic Page's tap ability during combat, which would give an attacking creature +1/+1 at no mana cost. With the opponent's creatures all having summoning sickness and unable to block, this is free extra damage. Additionally, Feat of Resistance could have been cast to permanently add a +1/+1 counter to an attacker.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Angelic Page or casting Feat of Resistance during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Angelic Page to give an attacking creature (likely Baneslayer Angel or Emancipation Angel) +1/+1 for free extra damage. Could also consider casting Feat of Resistance on Baneslayer Angel for a permanent +1/+1 counter.

annotations.description: Declined to chump block Baneslayer Angel (5/5 flying, first strike, lifelink) with a 0/1 Wispweaver Angel illusion token, taking 5 damage (32→27) and allowing opponent to gain 5 life (21→26). While the 0/1 tokens have some future value with Preston's blink/illusion synergies, trading a 0/1 body to save 5 life is usually worthwhile.
annotations.actionTaken: No blocks declared, taking 5 damage from Baneslayer Angel.
annotations.betterLine: Block Baneslayer Angel with one of the 0/1 Wispweaver Angel tokens to prevent 5 damage. The token has minimal combat value and preserving 5 life points is likely more important than keeping a 0/1 body for future blink synergies.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Angelic Page to pump Baneslayer Angel during combat. Baneslayer is attacking unblocked (all opponent's creatures have summoning sickness), so tapping Angelic Page would give +1/+1, dealing 6 damage instead of 5 and gaining 6 life instead of 5, at zero cost since Page isn't attacking.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Angelic Page
annotations.betterLine: Activate Angelic Page targeting Baneslayer Angel to get +1 damage and +1 life for free. Feat of Resistance could also be considered for a permanent +1/+1 counter, but at minimum the Page activation is pure upside.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Angelic Page (free tap ability) to give attacking Baneslayer Angel +1/+1, missing 1 extra damage and 1 extra life from lifelink for no cost. The opponent has no attackers coming back (all creatures are summoning sick), so tapping the 1/1 Page has zero defensive downside.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Angelic Page or casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Angelic Page to give Baneslayer Angel +1/+1 until end of turn, dealing 6 damage instead of 5 and gaining 6 life instead of 5.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Angelic Page to pump the attacking Baneslayer Angel for free. Angelic Page can tap (no mana cost) to give an attacking creature +1/+1, which would have dealt 1 extra damage and gained 1 extra life via lifelink. The opponent has no untapped blockers and almost no open mana for tricks.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Angelic Page or casting Feat of Resistance.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Angelic Page targeting Baneslayer Angel to get a free +1/+1 pump, dealing 6 damage instead of 5 and gaining 6 life instead of 5. Could also consider Feat of Resistance for a permanent +1/+1 counter.

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach declined to block a 4/4 flying Angel Token, taking 4 unnecessary damage. They had Feat of Resistance in hand with 3 untapped lands available, which could have given Emancipation Angel (3/3) a +1/+1 counter and protection from white. This would have made Emancipation Angel a 4/4 that takes no damage from the white Angel Token (protection prevents damage), killing the attacker for free while keeping their creature and gaining a permanent +1/+1 counter.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 4 damage (26 → 22 life).
annotations.betterLine: Block the 4/4 Angel Token with Emancipation Angel, then cast Feat of Resistance on Emancipation Angel choosing protection from white. This kills the Angel Token, saves Emancipation Angel (now a 4/4 with protection from white), and preserves 4 life.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Feat of Resistance during combat when an opponent's 4/4 Angel Token is attacking. Using Feat on Emancipation Angel (making it 4/4 with protection from white) would let it block and kill the white Angel Token while surviving, gaining both a permanent +1/+1 counter and destroying the opponent's token for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Feat of Resistance during combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Feat of Resistance targeting Emancipation Angel, choose protection from white, then block the 4/4 Angel Token. Emancipation Angel becomes 4/4, takes no damage from the white token due to protection, and the token dies. Net result: permanent +1/+1 counter on Emancipation Angel and opponent loses their 4/4 flyer.

annotations.description: Angelic Page can tap for free to give the unblocked Griffin Token +1/+1, dealing 3 damage instead of 2. There's no cost or downside since the Page isn't attacking or needed for anything else.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using Angelic Page's ability
annotations.betterLine: Tap Angelic Page to give Griffin Token +1/+1, dealing 1 extra damage for free

annotations.description: Angelic Page's +1/+1 pump was used on the Griffin Token (unblocked 2/2) instead of Baneslayer Angel (unblocked 5/5 with lifelink). Pumping Baneslayer would deal 6 damage and gain 6 life instead of 5/5, a 2-point swing in life differential. Pumping Griffin Token only adds 1 extra damage. The difference is 1 point of value (the extra lifelink).
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Griffin Token with Angelic Page's +1/+1 pump ability
annotations.betterLine: Target Baneslayer Angel with Angelic Page's pump to get +1 damage AND +1 life from lifelink, maximizing the 2-point life differential swing

annotations.description: Passed priority during combat with Feat of Resistance in hand and 5 untapped lands, missing the opportunity to put a permanent +1/+1 counter on Baneslayer Angel (making it 6/6) while it's attacking unblocked. Opponent's lands are all tapped, so there's no risk. This wastes a free +1 damage, +1 life from lifelink, and a permanent stat boost on the best creature on the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Feat of Resistance during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Feat of Resistance targeting Baneslayer Angel, choosing protection from white (or any relevant color), gaining a permanent +1/+1 counter and dealing 6 lifelink damage instead of 5.

annotations.description: Passed priority during combat with Feat of Resistance in hand and 5 untapped lands. Could have cast Feat of Resistance on Baneslayer Angel (unblocked attacker) to permanently buff it to 6/6, deal 1 extra damage, and gain 1 extra life. The opponent has all lands tapped so there's no risk of a blowout. The permanent +1/+1 counter on Baneslayer is meaningful ongoing value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything during combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Feat of Resistance targeting Baneslayer Angel, choosing protection from white. This permanently buffs Baneslayer to 6/6, deals 1 extra damage and gains 1 extra life this combat, and the protection could be relevant against the opponent's white creatures/removal.

annotations.description: Cast Bulwark Giant for 6 mana (gaining 5 life, getting a 3/6) when Brightmare for 3 mana could tap down Emiel the Blessed (gaining 4 life from its 4 power) while leaving 3 mana open for Feat of Resistance or other responses. The opponent has a dangerous flicker engine with Preston + Emiel + Distinguished Conjurer, and tapping Emiel would significantly reduce their ability to generate value next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bulwark Giant for {5}{W}, using all available mana for a 3/6 body and 5 life.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Brightmare targeting Emiel the Blessed to tap it and gain 4 life, leaving 3 mana open for Feat of Resistance to protect Baneslayer Angel or another key creature if needed. This provides nearly the same life gain, better tempo by neutralizing Emiel for a turn, and keeps mana available for interaction.

annotations.description: Targeted Baneslayer Angel (already tapped) with Brightmare's ETB for 5 life, but Baneslayer can't block this turn anyway. Tapping an untapped opponent creature like Basri's Acolyte or Anointed Chorister would gain less life (2) but remove a blocker, potentially enabling better attacks this turn. With multiple attackers available, removing a blocker could have been more impactful than the extra 3 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted the already-tapped Baneslayer Angel for 5 life gain
annotations.betterLine: Target Basri's Acolyte (untapped 2/3 lifelink) to tap it and prevent it from blocking, enabling more profitable attacks this combat. The 3 less life gained could be offset by better combat outcomes.
